topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the topic of complement and frames the scope and challenges of the lecture.

topics.label: Fundamentals of complement and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the general architecture of the complement cascade, its nomenclature conventions, and the central function of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the three recognition pathways that detect pathogens and deposit activated C3 on their surfaces to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the downstream effector processes through which activated complement eradicates pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It explains how deficiencies in different complement components lead to distinct clinical disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the strategies evolved by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
